queries.Primary analytical strategy for resolvin: solution-state NMR spectroscopy to determine substrate specificity and cleavage sites of Staphylococcus aureus lysostaphin and LytM peptidoglycan hydrolases using isotopically labeled pentaglycine synthetic peptides and real-time kinetic monitoring of hydrolysis products
queries.Substrate panel design for testing recog: Synthetic peptidoglycan peptide substrates with pentaglycine cross-bridge scaffolds for determining cleavage specificity of Staphylococcus aureus lysostaphin and LytM metalloendopeptidases
queries.Isotopic symmetry-breaking and cleavage-: Selective 13C 15N labeling of Gly2 C-alpha CO carbons in pentaglycine for NMR cleavage-site assignment using glycine-optimized 2D HA(CA)CO experiments to distinguish C-terminal non-terminal carbonyl resonances in Staphylococcus aureus lysostaphin LytM peptidoglycan hydrolase substrate specificity studies
queries.Real-time NMR kinetic monitoring and hyd: quantitative real-time 1H NMR kinetic monitoring of lysostaphin and LytM peptidoglycan hydrolysis of 13C-labeled pentaglycine substrates with multidimensional NMR product identification using HSQC HMBC and glycine-optimized 2D HA(CA)CO experiments
queries.Systematic kinetic comparison across pep: Systematic kinetic comparison of peptidoglycan fragment hydrolysis by Staphylococcus aureus lysostaphin and LytM using synthetic pentaglycine and cross-linked stem peptide substrates, quantitative NMR monitoring, substrate specificity and cleavage site determination
queries.Native sacculus validation by muropeptid: NMR analysis of native Staphylococcus aureus USA300 sacculus muropeptides extracted using SDS, DNase, Pronase, HCl, mutanolysin protocols, before and after lysostaphin LytM digestion, to confirm pentaglycine cross-bridge cleavage sites
queries.Living-cell validation of enzyme activit: Turbidity reduction assay measuring optical density at 600 nm over 16 hours for Staphylococcus aureus USA300 late stationary phase cells treated with lysostaphin-like peptidoglycan hydrolase at 50 micrograms per milliliter to validate living-cell enzyme activity
queries.Resistance-relevant substrate variation: Effects of cross-bridge length variations and serine substitutions in synthetic Staphylococcus aureus peptidoglycan peptides on lysostaphin and LytM hydrolysis and resistance mutant phenotypes
queries.Standardized experimental conditions and: NMR kinetic analysis of peptidoglycan hydrolase activity using 800 MHz quantitative 1H NMR at 25°C, initial rate linear regression and Michaelis-Menten fitting for Staphylococcus aureus lysostaphin and LytM pentaglycine substrate hydrolysis
